change: GET, PUT and DELETE /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/assistant/image-provider refuse an OAuth client other than Peal's command line (403 Forbidden, missingPermission assistant:configure), whatever its scopes
reason: Since the image provider endpoints shipped (2026-11-12), an application connected with workspace:write could point a workspace's image prompts, and now its drafts, at a server of its own, which kept receiving them after its grant was revoked. assistant:configure now reaches no OAuth client but Peal's command line; owners and admins in their own session, the command line, and API keys or partner keys given the permission keep it. An application that set a provider asks the person to set it in the web app, or uses an API key given assistant:configure.

change: The SDKs' BadGatewayErrorBody (one type for every 502 body with several errors) names TextProviderRefused and AssistantFailed, no longer AssistantFailed and ImageProviderRefused; AssistantFailedEncoded lost its _tag field, and its tag type (AssistantFailedEncodedTag, AssistantFailedEncoded.Tag) is gone
reason: The suggestions endpoint and the text provider's test now answer 502 with two errors each, and the generator names a single body type for each status, after one of the endpoints that has a union there. Nothing changes on the wire: every 502 body still carries its _tag. Code that matched BadGatewayErrorBody.ImageProviderRefused, or read AssistantFailedEncoded's _tag through its type, reads the body's _tag as a string instead. The SDKs are 0.x: this ships in their next minor release, 0.4.0, whose notes say so.

change: A post.cancelled webhook may name one channel taken off a post that still goes out on its others (scope: "target"), as well as a cancelled post (scope: "post")
reason: Removing one channel from a scheduled post (DELETE …/posts/{postId}/targets/{targetId}) is told as a post.cancelled naming that channel alone, as a channel cancelled while its post was going out already was. A receiver that marked the whole post cancelled on every post.cancelled reads the new scope field: "target" means the post still goes out on its other channels. Events made before the field was sent have none, and are about the post.

change: The SDKs' 402 error (PaymentRequiredError) no longer carries a typed PlanLimitReachedEncoded body on any endpoint: its body is untyped, and PaymentRequiredErrorBody (PlanLimitReachedEncoded or UsageAllowanceReachedEncoded) is the type to read it as; Rust's ApiError::PaymentRequiredError lost its fields (tag, code, request_id, allowed, billing_url, limit, plan, plan_with_room, used)
reason: Four endpoints (suggestions, images, an inbox reply, a boost) now answer 402 with two errors, PlanLimitReached and UsageAllowanceReached, and the generator names a single body type for each status, as for 502 before. Nothing changes on the wire: every 402 body still carries its _tag and the same fields, billingUrl included. Code that read PaymentRequiredError.body's fields through its type reads the body's _tag, then the fields, as PaymentRequiredErrorBody. The SDKs are 0.x: this ships in their next minor release, whose notes say so.

change: On a server that bills, POST …/assistant/suggestions and POST …/assistant/images answer 402 UsageAllowanceReached to a billing account without a payment method (paymentMethodRequired), where a daily quota answered before, and past the month's allowance or ceiling to one that pays
reason: The writing assistant on the server's models is a meter of the billing account (wave T, part T7): it needs a payment method, includes a monthly allowance, and bills past it up to a ceiling. A workspace's own text or image provider is not metered; a legacy plan keeps its daily quota; a server that does not bill is unchanged.

change: On a server that bills, POST …/inbox/comments/{commentId}/replies and POST …/ads/boosts may answer 402 UsageAllowanceReached once the billing account used the inbox messages or managed ads its month allows without a payment method, or on a legacy plan, or while its payment fails
reason: Outbound messages and managed ads are meters of the billing account (T7). Reading, publishing and running boosts are never metered; a reply sent again under its Idempotency-Key answers the reply it made.

change: On a server that bills, POST …/channels/connect/{platform}, …/callback and …/accounts answer 402 UsageAllowanceReached (meter xApi) to connect an X account when the billing account is not on per-account pricing that pays (paymentMethodRequired without a payment method, paymentFailed while its payment fails, planAllowance on a plan from before per-account pricing)
reason: X bills each call to its API, which Peal passes through at X's published rates, with nothing added: only a billing account that can be billed connects an X account. Reconnecting is never refused, existing channels stay, and a server that does not bill refuses nothing.

change: On a server that bills, a post's target on X may fail, nothing sent, with the failure reasons paymentMethodRequired, paymentFailed, perAccountPricingRequired or xCeilingReached, and a thread on X refused at a later part with xThreadCut, where it went out before; X's reads are billed only for a workspace that turned them on (PUT …/billing/x), and stop at the account's x ceiling
reason: X's posts and reads are billed at X's rates on the xApi meter, within the billing account's monthly ceiling for X. A server that does not bill publishes and reads X as before.

change: Channel.platform was a Platform, and is a ChannelPlatform
reason: A channel now connects a social network or a website (a self-hosted WordPress site), so its platform is a ChannelPlatform: every Platform value, plus wordpress. Nothing a client knew changes on the wire: a social channel answers the value it did, and a website's channel answers wordpress, which an SDK released before reads as a value it does not know, without failing. Platform stays the social networks' list everywhere else, the channels list's platform filter included, so no request takes wordpress where it would be refused. Upgrading an SDK changes the field's type from Platform to ChannelPlatform. TypeScript: compare channel.platform with the same strings; a variable typed Platform takes it once the value is checked to be a social network, or is typed ChannelPlatform. Go: compare with peal.ChannelPlatformX and its kin, not peal.PlatformX, which no longer compiles there. Rust: match ChannelPlatform::X and its kin, with an arm for the others. .NET: compare with ChannelPlatform.X, not Platform.X, which no longer compiles there. Java: Platform.X.equals(channel.getPlatform()) still compiles and is now always false: compare with ChannelPlatform.X, or the values' strings (toString()), and review every equals or switch on the field. Python, PHP and Ruby read the field as a string, and need no change.

change: Every endpoint that takes query parameters refuses one it does not take (400 InvalidRequest, field query.<name>) instead of ignoring it
reason: A misspelt filter, such as channelIds for channelId on GET …/posts/search, answered as if it applied: every post of the workspace, with a 200, which a script would then act on. The document already listed each endpoint's parameters, and the SDKs and the command line send only those. Endpoints without query parameters, the health checks among them, still take any query, and request bodies are read as before.

change: Every text field that refused a NUL character (a post's text, a channel's own text, alt text, options' text, signatures, recycling variants, follow-up and comment rules, review comments) also refuses an unpaired surrogate (400 InvalidRequest, "Expected text without NUL characters or unpaired surrogates")
reason: Postgres keeps an unpaired surrogate, half an emoji that a client cut by UTF-16 units, as U+FFFD: the API answered the text as sent and stored, and would publish, another one. A client that sends well-formed text is unchanged; one that cuts text cuts on code points.

change: The names a member writes (a tag, a signature, a channel set, a queue, a channel's label) refuse a mark that overrides, embeds or isolates their direction (U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069): 400 InvalidRequest, "Expected a name on one line, without control characters or marks that override its direction"
reason: A name is shown beside other text, to every member: such a mark reverses or hides what follows it (the "Trojan Source" marks of Unicode's security guidance). Left-to-right and right-to-left marks, which a right-to-left name may need, and the zero-width joiner of an emoji stay taken; names saved before keep what they hold.

change: POST /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/media/{mediaId}/complete waits up to 20 seconds while the workspace has two uploaded files probed at once, or the server eight, then answers 429 MediaImportBusy: the upload is completed and the media left uploaded, for the next call to probe
reason: Each call probed the file again, reading it whole or running ffprobe for up to a minute, with nothing bounding how many ran at once: a member calling it in a loop could exhaust the server's memory. Probes now take slots, as imports do; a client asks again in a moment.

change: POST /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/media/{mediaId}/complete no longer probes again media whose probe refused it as tooLarge or tooManyPages, an image or a document found unreadable, or a video found unreadable three times in a row: it answers the media as it stands
reason: Those refusals come from the file's bytes, which never change once stored, so probing again only repeated them, at the cost of reading the file each time; ffprobe reads a video from the store, so a failing store looks the same, and a video is read again a few times first. A client uploads the file again instead.

change: POST /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations answers 409 TooManyInvitations, its message saying so, once the member who invites, the workspace, the workspace for the address invited or the address across Peal had all the invitation emails a day (UTC) allows: 100, 100, 3 and 20
reason: Every invitation sends an email from Peal's own domain naming its inviter and its workspace, which made invitations a relay for unwanted mail. The code stays the one a workspace with too many pending invitations answered already.

change: POST and DELETE /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations, and GET …/invitations, refuse an OAuth client other than Peal's command line (403 Forbidden, missingPermission invitation:create or invitation:cancel), whatever its scopes; so do the other endpoints that take member:create, member:update or member:delete
reason: An application connected with workspace:write could invite an address it holds as an admin, or an owner, whose new member held everything the grant withheld and stayed once it was revoked. Who is in a workspace, and as what, now reaches no OAuth client but Peal's command line; members in their own session, the command line, and API keys or partner keys given the permissions keep them. The MCP endpoint no longer offers invite_member, list_invitations or revoke_invitation.

change: Every endpoint answers 413 payload_too_large to a body past 1 MiB, but those under /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/posts and /articles, which take 8 MiB; Better Auth's routes under /api/auth answer 413 to a body declared past 1 MiB
reason: No endpoint but four had a limit, so any route, those without credentials included, read whatever it was sent, up to Bun's 128 MiB. Media goes to the bucket, never through the server; a bulk request of 50 posts or a CSV import of a million characters stays well under 8 MiB.

change: Every address whose path holds a semicolon, raw or encoded (%3B, any case), answers 400 bad_request before any route runs
reason: The proxy in front of Peal drops what follows a semicolon in a segment before it picks the rule that says whether Access guards a path, so /api/admin/users/..;/..;/api/health was an open path to it and the staff console to the router. No route takes a semicolon; a query may still hold one.

change: POST /api/partner/workspaces and PATCH /api/partner/workspaces/{workspaceId} answer 422 InvalidWorkspaceDetails (field name) for a name holding `://` or `www.`, and keep a name on one line, without the marks that reorder it
reason: A workspace's name goes into the emails Peal sends from its own domain; it is now kept as Better Auth's routes keep a member's workspace's name. Names saved before keep what they hold, and emails leave out any name that reads as a web or email address.

change: An API key made from now on stops working (401) once the member who made it leaves the workspace, is removed from it or closes their account, and once their role is changed to one that could not give one of the key's permissions; keys made before stay
reason: A key outlived the member who made it, with everything they held, and with no expiry: a member about to be removed or demoted could keep their access through a key. A key now records its maker (ApiKey.createdBy), and follows their standing in the workspace.

change: A partner key whose maker is recorded stops working (401) once they leave the partner's home workspace, are removed from it or close their account, and once their role there no longer holds partner:manage; keys whose maker closed their account before stay
reason: A partner key outlived the admin who made it, across every customer workspace: an admin about to be removed kept access through it. Partner keys now follow their maker as API keys do, and PartnerKey.createdBy names them.
